https://github.com/sergiomanzur/Symphony.body:
Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, running natively on Android. Not an emulator — the
PlayStation code is statically recompiled into C# and built into a real app.

A fix release on top of Beta 0.10, all of it about save states and controllers.
Tested on a Retroid Pocket 6.

---

## Fixed

**Loading a save state now restores the music.** This is the big one, and it had two
separate causes stacked on top of each other.

Three quarters of this disc is streamed audio — 172,972 of its 229,020 sectors — so on SOTN
the soundtrack is not sequenced, it is read off the disc as you play. Which track you hear
depends on where the drive is sitting and which channel it is filtering. None of that was
part of a save state. So loading one restored the game's memory while leaving the drive
exactly where the current session had left it, and the game had no reason to re-issue a read
it believed it had already made.

The result was oddly specific: load a state from the main menu and the menu's theme carried
on playing over the restored room. Walk into the next room and it corrected itself, because
that made the game ask the drive for music again. From a freshly launched app the drive could
still be near the start of the disc, where the first streamed audio is the game's opening
narration — so a boss room could greet you with Richter's opening line, which is at least
funny.

The drive's position, channel filter and mode are now saved and restored with the state.

**Sound effects and voices no longer come back wrong.** The same absence, one layer down. The
PlayStation's sound chip has its own half-megabyte of sample memory, and the game fills it
once when you enter an area; after that it only says "play the sample at this address". A
save state restored the game's bookkeeping about which sample was where, but not the samples
themselves — so those addresses still resolved, just to whatever the previous session had
loaded. The sample memory, all 24 voices and the mixer registers now travel with the state.

Two earlier attempts at this fought it from the wrong side, by resetting or silencing the
sound chip on load. One left the game permanently mute; the other kept the volume but stopped
the music. Neither could have worked, because the state simply was not there to restore. It is
now.

**A controller connected after the game is already running is picked up.** Reported with a
wired USB-C pad, but it was never about that pad — nothing attached after startup was ever
noticed. The only scan happened once during launch, before Android had finished enumerating
its input devices, so a pad was found by luck. Built-in controls usually got lucky; a USB-C
pad, which you plug into a phone that is already running, never did. Connecting and
disconnecting are both noticed within a frame now.

**A controller no longer takes the game down with it.** Opening certain pads makes the input
layer leave a harmless complaint behind — the pad opens and works fine — but that message is
sticky, and the layer above treats any pending message as a failure. The frame after a
controller was opened could die and stop the game.

---

## Added

**⚙ MENU → System → Controllers.** A pad that does nothing has more than one cause: the
system never saw it, or it was seen but has no button mapping and cannot be driven. From the
outside those look identical. This screen lists every controller the system reports, marks
each *Usable* or *No button mapping*, shows which player slots are filled, and can scan again
without restarting. If a pad still misbehaves, photograph this screen for the bug report.

Save and load results are also written to the device log now. Previously a failure appeared
only as a toast, which is gone by the time anyone thinks to describe what happened.

---

## Worth knowing

**Your existing save states still work.** States from 0.10 have no drive section and load
exactly as they did before; states from before 0.10 have neither. Only states written by this
version get the full treatment, so re-save anything you care about if you want the music fix
to apply to it.

Save states are a little larger again — the sound chip's sample memory adds about half a
megabyte on top of the roughly 8 MB each slot already used.

Memory cards are unaffected.

This one catches the port up to upstream's **Beta 0.5.1b**, which is mostly a widescreen

---

## Widescreen is properly widescreen now

Beta 0.9.1 made the game *render* wider instead of stretching a 4:3 picture sideways. That
fixed how it looked, but the game underneath still only reasoned about the original view.
Upstream has since reworked that part, and this release brings it over.

**Enemies now spawn and can be hit at the edges of the screen.** Spawning, hit detection and
camera collision are handled for the widened view itself rather than being nudged afterwards.
Previously things could walk into frame already resolved, or sit in the extra space at the
sides without properly existing.

**Backgrounds stop losing chunks of tile in widescreen.** The PlayStation had 2 MB of work
RAM and the widescreen hooks run out of it while building the extra tile columns a wider view
needs. The emulated console now gets 8 MB, which is what upstream raised it to for the same
reason.

**The Prologue throne room is filled in.** Widening that room exposed empty space to the left
of the throne, and the artwork that covers it was never being drawn on Android.

**Inverted castle screen bounds are correct**, which upstream fixed separately.

---

## Controllers

**A pad connected after the game is already running now works.** This was reported with a
wired USB-C controller, and it was never about that particular pad — on Android *nothing*
attached after startup was ever picked up. The only scan happened once during launch, before
Android had even finished enumerating its input devices, so a pad was found by luck. Built-in
controls like the Retroid's usually got lucky. A USB-C pad, which you plug into a phone that
is already running, never did.

Connecting and disconnecting are both noticed within a frame now, with no restart.

**A controller no longer takes the game down with it.** Opening certain pads makes SDL leave a
harmless complaint in its error slot — the pad opens and works fine. But that message is
sticky, and the layer above throws on *any* pending error, whether or not its own call failed.
So the frame after a controller was opened could die and stop the game. This is the more likely
reason a specific controller looked like it "wasn't recognised": with the pad attached at
launch, the same trap could leave the app running with nothing on screen.

**New: ⚙ MENU → System → Controllers.** A pad that does nothing has more than one cause — the
system never saw it, or it was seen but has no button mapping and so cannot be driven — and
from the outside those look the same. This screen lists every controller the system reports,
marks each *Usable* or *No button mapping*, shows which player slots are filled, and can scan
again without restarting. If a pad still misbehaves, this is the screen to photograph in a bug
report.

I don't own the controller this was reported with, so the wired path was verified with a
synthetic USB gamepad on the device rather than the real thing.

---

## Changed

**High resolution is now a render scale picker** (⚙ MENU → System → Display → Render scale),
following upstream replacing its own on/off toggle with a slider. The old switch could only
say 1x or 4x; on a phone 2x is often the better trade between a clean picture and battery.
It applies immediately — no restart, unlike the desktop build.

## Also from upstream

Minotaur and Werewolf crash fix. Soft reset now returns to the title screen properly.
Japanese and Simplified Chinese interface translations. Fixes to the GTE, the sound processor's
note handling, interrupt dispatch, and a stale frame that could linger after a video. CHD disc
images are supported by the runtime, though the importer here still asks for cue/bin.

Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, running natively on Android. Not an emulator — the

A fix release on top of Beta 0.9, tested on a Retroid Pocket 6.

---

## Fixed

**16:9 and fit-to-screen no longer stretch the picture.** Choosing a wider ratio used to
widen the rectangle the frame was drawn into without changing the frame itself, so a 4:3
picture was pulled sideways to fill it. The game now genuinely *renders* wider, so widescreen
shows more of the level instead of a distorted version of the same view.

The aspect modes now mean what they say:

- **4:3 original** — the framing the game was made for
- **16:9 widescreen** — true 16:9, more level visible left and right
- **Fit device** — renders at your screen's own ratio, filling it exactly with no bars
- **Stretch to fill** — still stretches, for anyone who wants it

**Glitched text and warped sprites are gone.** Both were the stretching above: scaling
unevenly duplicates some pixel columns and not others, which breaks up small text and makes
a symmetrical object's edges disagree. Nothing looks squashed now, so neither happens.

**The d-pad no longer presses L1 or L2 with it.** The movement and action pads are
hit-tested by radius, and that radius reached past their artwork into the shoulder buttons
above — while nothing stopped a single touch from matching more than one control. Pressing
Up would fire L2 along with it, since L2 sits directly above. One touch now activates one
control, and the shoulders sit further clear of the pad.

**Audio delay roughly halved.** The buffer was pinned at a tenth of a second no matter what
the device could manage. It now sizes itself from the device's own minimum and asks for the
platform's low-latency path where that exists.

**Audio crackling fixed.** Separate cause: the mixer ran as an ordinary background thread, so
Android's scheduler could interrupt it mid-frame and the sound buffer would run dry between
writes. It now runs at the priority the system reserves for audio.

---

## Added

**Import and export memory cards**, under **⚙ MENU → Save → Memory cards**.

Saves live in the app's private storage, so until now there was no way to back one up, move
it to another device, or bring one over from the desktop build.

- **Export** writes the card anywhere you choose, and flushes the live card first so it is
  never a save behind what you just did
- **Import** accepts the raw 128 KB card used by `.mcr`, `.mcd` and `.sav`, plus DexDrive and
  VGS files
- A file that is not a formatted card is refused rather than written, so a mis-tap cannot
  wipe a save, and the card being replaced is kept beside the new one
- The app restarts after importing, which is what makes the imported card load

## You need your own copy of the game

**This APK contains no game data, and never will.** You need a legally owned copy of the
North American PlayStation release, dumped to `.cue` + `.bin`.

On first launch the app asks for it. Select the `.cue` and **both** `.bin` tracks together —

Your files can be named anything. The importer reads your `.cue`, pulls in exactly the tracks
it names, and rewrites it to match. It also checks the disc really is the USA release, and
tells you if you've handed it a Japanese or European dump by mistake.

## What's in it

- **Touch controls** — full PSX overlay, switchable D-pad or virtual stick, adjustable
  opacity, and a HIDE toggle that gets the buttons out of the way
- **Physical controllers** — Bluetooth, USB and handhelds (Retroid, Odin, Xbox, DualSense),
  with PlayStation / Xbox / Nintendo button layouts
- **Save states** — five slots
- **Quality of life** — colour blind fixes, remove screen flashes, bug fixes, easy spell
  inputs, extra invincibility frames and more
- **Cheats, stats and inventory** — heal, level, gold, attributes, and a full item, relic and
  spell editor
- **Mods** — compiled on device, so source mods work as they do on desktop
- **Display** — 4:3, 16:9, stretch or auto-fit, with orientation lock; settings persist

Everything lives behind the **⚙ MENU** button in the top corner.

---

## Known limitations

- **Save states are best used within one session.** The emulated sound chip isn't captured in
  a state, so one loaded in a different area can play the wrong samples until the game
  reloads them.
- The map tracker and randomizer panels are desktop-only for now.

What's new:


📲 UI
\- Completely rewrote the UI using Jetpack Compose.

🖥️ Renderer Backend

\- Added a new EGLRenderer.
\- Improved the overall performance of the VulkanRenderer and added ReShade support.

\- Added DisplayX, a new implementation based on SurfaceFlinger for native composition.
\- Provides support for the Android Hardware Composer (HWC).
\- Supports the Android Performance Hint API.
\- Supports an X Server bypass, allowing DisplayX to bypass the traditional X Server composition path.
\- DisplayX is currently experimental.

---

🖥️ X Server

\- Fixed a long-standing issue with X resource management.

\- Reworked the DRI3 and Pixmap extensions to provide proper direct rendering support.

\- Reworked the Drawable backend to allow hardware-accelerated Xlib buffers.

\- Added the GLX extension for Zink DRI3, allowing proper GPU-accelerated OpenGL rendering.

\- Added the XComposite extension for proper offscreen rendering support.

\- Improved Zink performance for OpenGL games, benefiting non-Adreno GPUs.

\- Added support for Freedreno, the Powerful OpenGL driver for Adreno GPUs.

\- Freedreno can massively improve performance in OpenGL games.

📦 Proton & Assets

\- Updated all Proton assets.

\- Added support for:
 \- RandR
 \- XInput2
 \- XComposite

\- Added new Proton 9, Proton 10, and Proton 11 versions, Proton 10 and 11 are compatible with Fex Unixlibs

\- Playing OpenGL games using Proton 11 is currently not recommended.

🎮 On-Screen Controllers

\- Added support for custom icons and fixed bugs.

🖱️ Input

\- Fixed issues with relative mouse input.

🔊 Audio

\- Added GameNative PulseAudio.

📈 Modern HUD

\- Added GPU name detection and display.

\- Added several additional improvements and adjustments to the Modern HUD.

📝 Notes

As always, delete your old Ludashi build or change the package name. This version does not install as an update.

Bug fixes and improvements are planned for future updates.

Regarding Frame Generation and Steam support: no, they are not planned. However, I will release all the source code so other projects can use my features if they want.

Hello!

It's been a little while, so I thought I would just give a small update on project status. 

- Winlator Cmod development continues!
- My focus on next release will either be mostly QoL. This means addressing long standing bug fixes, but more importantly, **merging and crediting improvements from other forks of Cmod from trusted developers.** Primarily I'll be focused on:
- Fixing dynamic package name paths for the gamepad implementation so that name can be changed, such as adding a ludashi benchmark version with the SDL joystick native controller support.
- Input control / touch screen control bindings bug fixes
- Minor UI improvements and enhancements
- Updating all drivers, Fex, Box64, and graphics Wrapper, following Pipetto-Crypto's advice when it comes to Streamlining and avoiding feature creep (...and avoiding pure AI code slop). 
- Improve ALSA-Reflector so audio stops cutting out after 15 minutes unless you switch to headphones.

I'm leaning on this being v13.2. A v14 Cmod should be more substantial. Ultimately I would like to overhaul how Containers are created, with a focus on something more aligned and user friendly like Gamehub, such as starting the app and choosing a Windows based executable directly in the UI, then auto creating or maintain a single container or edge case containers. This would work well with something like Per Game Fixes, or a standardized compatibility list like what's on Reddit.  

Lastly, I'm sorry I'm not good about addressing Github issues. I just have not had any time. I am also looking forward to what Valve brings to the table with the Frame and it's ARM based Linux OS with Android app support. I imagine Proton is going to be getting some major improvements for ARM over the next year, so I don't see things slowing down much. Google seems to be walking back some of the unknown app restrictions they announced this year, so that's also good. Lots to look forward to. 

Stay Kazzy,
Goro Majima

https://github.com/coffincolors/winlator.name: Winlator Cmod v13: The Controller Revolution is Here! (And much more...)
https://github.com/coffincolors/winlator.body: The wait is over. After months of work the next major evolution of Winlator Cmod has arrived. I teased that a controller revolution was coming, but the reality is so much bigger. This isn't just an update; it's a top-to-bottom overhaul focused on bringing a native, seamless gaming experience to your device. This release is the culmination of a journey, and I'm proud to share it with you. ✨ What's New in Cmod v13 ✨ -------------------------- ### 🎮 The Controller Revolution: Native Gamepad Support is Here! The old input methods are gone (sorta), replaced by a completely new, from-the-ground-up controller implementation built on a native SDL2 backend. - **Native XInput & DInput Support:** No more switching settings per game! Controllers are now treated like real controllers. If it works on a PC, it should just work here. - **Multiplayer (Up to 4 Players!):** You heard that right. Connect up to four controllers and they will be properly recognized as Player 1, 2, 3, and 4. - **Vibration / Rumble:** Feel the action with full haptic feedback support. It can be toggled on or off. - **Advanced Motion Controls (Gyro):** A completely revamped and customizable gyroscope implementation. Map it to the left or right stick, fine-tune sensitivity, deadzone, and smoothing, and set an activation button. - **Turbo & Macros:** Set up autofire for any button (including triggers!) for each of your controllers. - **Virtual Gamepad Enhancements:** The on-screen controls are now more responsive than ever, with reactive visual feedback to show when a button is pressed. ### 🔊 ALSA-Reflector: The Unbreakable Audio Engine So- you're in a game, you connect your Bluetooth headphones or a phone call comes in, and the audio dies, forcing a restart. **Those days are over.** - **Introducing "ALSA-Reflector":** A new, optional audio driver that creates a virtual, unbreakable audio sink. It provides stable back-pressure to Wine, completely immune to Android's device changes. - **Seamless Recovery:** Real audio is mirrored to your hardware. If the connection breaks, the playback stream is automatically rebuilt in the background without interrupting the game's audio flow. The music never stops. # CEMU Android v0.5.2: Graphic Packs Custom Root Fix

Version 0.5.2 is a small maintenance release focused on graphic pack storage handling.

This release fixes how CEMU Android determines the graphic packs root directory. Graphic pack downloads and updates now use the active `CemuDataStorage` root when available, instead of always using Android's external app files directory.

This should make graphic pack management behave correctly when using **Data storage > Custom root**.

- Graphic packs now resolve their root directory through `CemuDataStorage`.
- Graphic pack downloads and updates now follow the active/custom storage root.
- Added fallback to the Android app external files directory when no active `CemuDataStorage` root is available.

## Notes

- `Use CemuDataStorage to determine graphic packs root directory`

No other emulator core, rendering, input, save sync, or external display changes are included in this release.

This release is based on the latest upstream Android port and adds several important improvements for save management, portable data, external displays, and Odin 2 support.

The main new feature is **external save file sync**, which makes it easier to use cloud sync, backups, or external synchronization tools with your CEMU save data.

This release also adds **Data storage > Custom root** support, allowing users to keep portable save data in a custom location.

And finally, **proper Odin 2 dual-screen support is here**.

Sorry for the wait on this one. I know Odin 2 users have been waiting for better support, and this release should make the experience much better.

---

## New Features:

* **External save file sync support**

  * Added support for syncing game save files through an external location.
  * This makes it easier to use cloud sync, backups, or external synchronization tools.
  * Game saves can now be kept in a more portable and user-accessible location.

* **Custom root support**

  * Added support for **Data storage > Custom root**.
  * This allows portable save data to be stored in a custom root folder.
  * Useful for users who want more control over where CEMU stores save-related data.

* **Automatic game save sync**

  * Game saves are synchronized automatically.
  * This should make external save workflows easier and safer to use.

* **Manual portable data import/export**

  * Settings, graphic packs, logs, and other portable data can be imported or exported manually.
  * This gives users more control over what data is moved or backed up.

* **External display support**

  * Added support for external displays.
  * Improved behavior when using CEMU with a second screen.

* **Screen swapping support**

  * Added screen swapping support.
  * This is useful for dual-screen and external display setups.

* **Proper Odin 2 dual-screen support**

  * Added proper dual-screen support for Odin 2.
  * This should make the Odin 2 experience much better for users using dual-screen layouts or external display setups.

---

## Save Sync and Portable Data:

This release improves how CEMU Android handles save data and portable files.

Game saves now support external sync, which can help users who want to:

* Sync saves with cloud storage.
* Keep backups outside app storage.
* Use external synchronization tools.
* Move saves more easily between devices.
* Keep save data in a custom root folder.

Game saves are synchronized automatically.

Other portable data, such as settings, graphic packs, logs, and related files, can be imported or exported manually.

---

## Odin 2 Support:

This release finally adds proper Odin 2 dual-screen support.

Sorry for the delay.

Odin 2 users should now have a much better experience with dual-screen layouts, screen swapping, and external display usage.

Please test your games and layouts, especially if you use external displays or custom screen setups.

The signing key changed for this release.

Because of that, Android may refuse to install CEMU Android v0.5.1 over a previous build.

If Android refuses to update:

1. Back up your saves first, especially if they are still only stored inside app storage.
2. Uninstall the old version.
3. Install CEMU Android v0.5.1.
4. Restore or reconfigure your save sync / custom root setup if needed.

Please do not uninstall the old version until your saves are backed up or synced externally.

---

This release is focused on save portability, external display workflows, Odin 2 support, and keeping the Android port closer to the latest upstream work.

Please report any issues with:

* Device model
* Android version
* Game name
* Storage mode used
* Custom root path setup

* Steps to reproduce the issue
* Screenshots or videos if possible

# **Mjolnir v0.2.6a — HOTFIX: Preventing a Rare Soft-Lock Scenario**

### **Update Safety Summary**

* **If you're on any 0.2.5 build:**
  ➜ **Upgrade immediately.**
* **If you're on 0.2.4h or earlier stable:**
  ➜ **0.2.6a is safe to upgrade to.**
* **If you specifically want the Emergency Recovery Panel:**
  ➜ That feature arrives in **v0.2.6b**. You may stay on **0.2.4h** until then if you prefer.

---

# **What Happened? (HOTFIX Context)**

A small number of users on **Basic Mode** discovered a rare edge case:

* If one screen was assigned a frontend
* And the other screen was assigned `<Nothing>`
* And the device rebooted

…Android would attempt to launch Mjolnir with only one valid Activity target.

This resulted in:

* A black or frozen display on one screen
* Inability to launch Settings
* Inability to change default launcher
* Inability to open Mjolnir itself
* Inability to uninstall 
* Under specific conditions, inability to recover at all without a factory reset

This was internally called the **“Bottomless Pit”** configuration.

**v0.2.6a fixes this completely.**
It prevents users from entering this configuration, detects it at startup if already present, and forces a safe recovery.

---

# **What’s Fixed in v0.2.6a**

## **1. Panic & State Handlers**

### **• Automatic Invalid Config Detection (Basic Mode)**

If Mjolnir detects that Basic Mode is missing a required app on either screen, it now:

* clears the invalid config,
* prevents the pit from forming,
* and cleanly reroutes the user to onboarding.

### **• Advanced Mode Save Fix**

In certain conditions, Advanced configurations were not being saved after returning from default-home settings. This caused inconsistent behavior.
This is now fully resolved — configuration always saves once requirements are met.

---

## **2. Onboarding Flow Hardening**

### **• Strict Basic Mode Completion**

The app picker in Basic Mode now requires **both** Top and Bottom selections before allowing you to continue.

### **• Required Permissions in Advanced Mode**

Notification and Accessibility permissions can no longer be skipped.
These are mandatory for correct Advanced behavior.

### **• Duplicate App Prevention**

Selecting an app already assigned to the opposite screen now swaps the two entries, preventing duplicate or invalid setups.

### **• Correct Default Home Logic**

The final onboarding step now correctly determines when a specific default launcher is required:

* Normal dual-frontend setups → **Any default launcher works**
* Bottom = `<Nothing>` → **Quickstep must be default**

---

## **3. UI & Quality Improvements**

### **• Markdown Rendering in “What’s New”**

Fixed an issue where markdown symbols and `\n` characters appeared literally.
Changelogs now display clean, formatted text.

### **• Safer Gesture Defaults**

New installs (or resets) now start with safe, functional gestures:

* **Tap → Both Home**
* **Double Tap → Top Home**
* **Triple Tap → Recents**
* **Long Press → Bottom Home**

These defaults help ensure users always have a recovery path.

---

# **Coming in v0.2.6b — The Emergency Recovery Panel**

v0.2.6a **prevents** invalid states.
**v0.2.6b will introduce a recovery tool for any state — even ones not yet discovered.**

Planned capabilities:

* Emergency recovery UI triggered by a gesture sequence
* Re-run onboarding
* Reset configuration
* Open Settings on either screen
* Export logs
* Attempt uninstall
* Enter a fallback safe-mode activity

This panel lives inside Mjolnir itself and does not rely on permissions or services, making it resilient even in extreme edge cases.

---

# **Should You Update? (Summary)**

* **On 0.2.5?**
  ➜ **Upgrade immediately.**
  (0.2.5 contains the soft-lock bug.)

* **On 0.2.4h/earlier?**
  ➜ **0.2.6a is safe and stable.**

* **Waiting for the Emergency Recovery Panel?**
  ➜ That arrives in **0.2.6b**. Staying on 0.2.4h until then is fine.

### v0.2.3 was a big update that addressed 2 major bugs.

1. "Clear all" would kill the Mjolnir process, and the service along with it. To fix this, I made a number of changes so that Mjolnir is no longer visible to the "Clear all" function and the service stays alive. This was a bug, and in v0.2.3 it's fixed.

2. Assigning the same app to both top and bottom screen would cause numerous bugs that would break input control when the user would send both screens home - so in v0.2.3, I removed the ability for users to assign the same screen as top and bottom. After all, that was never the intended purpose of Mjolnir.

But one user wanted the same app on top and bottom. So I turned the bug into a feature.

### v0.2.4b introduces Nothing.

- You can now assign Nothing to the top or bottom screen.
- As long as you have ONE frontend or launcher assigned to either Top or Bottom and Nothing in the other, the following occurs:

>  - Top Home sends your assigned app to the Top Screen
>  - Bottom Home sends your assigned app to the Bottom Screen
>  - Both Home sends your assigned app to whichever screen is selected as the Main Screen

 - **IT IS STRONGLY RECOMMENDED** to enable the experimental workaround if you're going to assign Nothing. There is a bug in AYN's Focus Lock that causes input to break, and the experimental workaround... works around it.

# Mjolnir v0.2.3 — Stability, Diagnostics & Quality of Life

This release focuses on **long-term stability**, **diagnostics**, and solving the biggest issue users reported:  
**Mjolnir dying when clearing all apps from Recents.**

## 🛠 Major Fix: Home Capture Now Survives “Clear All”
The Thor’s “Clear All” gesture used to kill Mjolnir outright.  
Not anymore.

Mjolnir’s Home interception service is now:
- Persistent  
- Isolated  
- Protected  
- Immune to Recents → Clear All  

Your Home gestures stay active no matter what.

## 🧪 New: Full Diagnostics Framework
A brand-new diagnostics system is included to help track down rare bugs.

- Toggle diagnostics on/off
- View, export, and delete logs
- Logs include gesture events, service lifecycle, notification state, settings snapshots, and more

All stored locally. No network access, no privacy concerns.

## 🎮 New Gesture Option: “Open Recents”
You can now assign the **App Switcher / Recents menu** to any Home gesture:
- Single tap  
- Double tap  
- Long press  

A highly-requested addition.

## 🧭 App Picker Improvements
- Fixed Quickstep and system apps not appearing in the full app list
- Implemented a functional **Blacklist** to prevent selecting apps that break the launcher workflow
- Added intelligent **slot-swap**: assigning the same app to both screens now swaps them instead of duplicating

## 🔧 General Improvements
- Dedicated :keepalive process for stronger persistence
- Reduced background overhead in keepalive process
- Improved notification text clarity
- Cleaner state reporting

## 🔭 What’s Next?
Mjolnir will soon receive an architectural refinement:  
A clean separation between the **stable launcher engine** and the **toolkit UI**.

This will make:
- The launcher even more reliable  
- Settings easier to access  
- Future tools easier to build  

For now, v0.2.3 is the most stable and capable version of Mjolnir yet.

Thank you to everyone who contacted me on Discord with issues, suggestions or just appreciation!
